aspects.says: asSubclass checks a loaded class against the expected type at once; an unchecked cast of the Class object checks nothing and the failure comes where an instance is used.
basis: section:A Class Named in Configuration Fails at First Use, Unless Startup Resolves It

aspects.says: Class.newInstance rethrows the constructor's exception as it is, so a checked exception escapes a catch of ReflectiveOperationException and the caller can't even catch it by type.
basis: section:Class.newInstance Lets the Constructor's Checked Exception Escape Undeclared

aspects.says: Constructor.newInstance wraps whatever the constructor throws in InvocationTargetException, whose cause is the constructor's own exception.
basis: section:Class.newInstance Lets the Constructor's Checked Exception Escape Undeclared

aspects.says: A static initialiser that throws gives ExceptionInInitializerError once; every later use of the class throws NoClassDefFoundError and the initialiser is not run again.
basis: section:Class.forName(name) Runs the Static Initialiser; the Three-Argument Form Waits for First Use

aspects.says: Class.forName(name) runs the class's static initialiser; forName(name, false, loader) and a class literal load without it, and the initialiser runs at first instance or static access.
basis: section:Class.forName(name) Runs the Static Initialiser; the Three-Argument Form Waits for First Use

aspects.says: findVirtual looks a method up by its full type, return type included, and a type that doesn't match fails at the lookup.
basis: section:A Method Handle Has a Type, and invokeExact Holds the Call Site to It

aspects.says: invokeExact compiles with any call-site types and throws WrongMethodTypeException at run time unless they equal the handle's type; invoke and asType adapt.
basis: section:A Method Handle Has a Type, and invokeExact Holds the Call Site to It

aspects.says: A class named in a string is looked up only when code asks for it, so a misspelt name fails at its first use unless startup resolves it.
basis: section:A Class Named in Configuration Fails at First Use, Unless Startup Resolves It
